questions.prompt: What are the two main categories of storage volumes in LXD?
options: Instance volumes (auto-created root disks) and custom volumes (user-created)
questions.answer: Instance volumes (auto-created root disks) and custom volumes (user-created)
questions.explanation: Instance volumes are created automatically when you launch an instance. Custom volumes are created by the user for shared or persistent data.

questions.prompt: How do you create a custom volume named 'data' in the 'default' pool?
options: lxc storage volume create default data
questions.answer: lxc storage volume create default data
questions.explanation: lxc storage volume create <pool> <name> creates a custom volume in the specified pool.

questions.prompt: How do you attach a custom volume 'data' to container 'web' at '/mnt/data'?
options: lxc storage volume attach default data web /mnt/data
lxc config device add web data disk source=default/data
questions.answer: lxc storage volume attach default data web /mnt/data
questions.explanation: lxc storage volume attach <pool> <volume> <instance> <mount-point> attaches a custom volume to an instance.

questions.prompt: What happens to a custom volume when the instance it's attached to is deleted?
options: The custom volume persists — it's independent of the instance
The custom volume is automatically deleted
The custom volume is detached but marked as read-only
The custom volume is converted to an image
questions.answer: The custom volume persists — it's independent of the instance
questions.explanation: Custom volumes are independent of instances. They persist until explicitly deleted, making them useful for data that must survive instance deletion.
